{{Trail}}{{TOCright}}[[File:ON-misc-Skills Menu.jpg|A player perusing the Skills menu|thumb|right]] In Elder Scrolls Online, you advance your character by using different abilities, granted to you through different skill lines. In order to increase your progression in a skill line, you must use those skills. There are three types of skills: Passive Skills, Active Skills, and Ultimate Skills. '''Passive Skills''' provide a bonus all the time. Some require certain items to be equipped or Active Skills to be slotted, but otherwise you don't need to think about them. They generally have a number of upgrades available, which can be acquired by increasing your level in the relevant skill line. In most cases, this is achieved by using the Active Skills within the same skill line. In other cases, such as crafting skills, this can be achieved via crafting items or research. Each upgrade costs an additional skill point. Some Passive Skills do not require an investment of skill points, but are instead provided free as a result of certain situations. For example, each [[ON:Races|race]] gets one free passive which increases their experience gain with a given skill. The first level of each of the [[ON:Crafting|Crafting]] quality skills is free. There are free Passive Skills associated with becoming a [[ON:Werewolf|Werewolf]] or [[ON:Vampire|Vampire]], as well as some provided by the keeps and resources owned by your [[ON:Alliance|Alliance]] if you take part in the [[ON:Alliance War|Alliance War]]. All current [[ON:Emperor|Emperor]]s also receive some free Passive Skills. '''Active Skills''' are the ones you'll be using most in the game. They cost either {{ESO Stamina Link|}} or {{ESO Magicka Link|}} to use. You can have up to five slotted in your Action Bar, by default bound to the 1-5 keys. At character level 15, when you acquire Weapon Swapping, you gain an additional 5 slots for your alternate weapon. Like Passive Skills, they become available once a certain level in the skill line is reached. However, they cannot be upgraded, but rather improve through use. They have 4 Ranks, after which they may be Morphed into a new version. You will have two Morph options, which add different effects to the skill. Morphing a skill costs an additional skill point. Once a skill is Morphed, it can increase in Rank 4 more times, but may not be Morphed again (so you can't get both Morph bonuses for any skill). Using your Active Skills will increase your overall level in the skill line, making new skills become available as you progress. '''Ultimate Skills''' are similar to Active Skills, but instead of using Stamina or Magicka as most Active Skills do, these use a third resource called [[ON:Ultimate|Ultimate]]. Ultimate builds over time as you fight, and (with [[ON:Overload|one exception]]) completely depletes when you perform an Ultimate Skill. No skill line has more than one Ultimate Skill, if it has one at all. Like Active Skills, they become available after a certain level in the skill line, raise in Ranks, and can be Morphed into new skills after Rank IV. You may only have one Ultimate Skill slotted at a time (two if you have Weapon Swapping after reaching level 15). By default it is bound to the 'R' key. ==Class== Each of the game's [[ON:Classes|classes]] has three skill lines associated with it, which are immediately available to your character and are specific to your class. To advance in the skill line, at least one active skill from the skill line must be slotted (as one of the regular five skills, or as the active Ultimate) on whichever of your two skill bars is in use at the moment of gaining experience points. {|class=hiddentable style="border-spacing: 1.5em 0.2em; text-align: center;" ![[ON:Dragonknight|Dragonknight]] ![[ON:Sorcerer|Sorcerer]] ![[ON:Nightblade|Nightblade]] ![[ON:Templar|Templar]] ![[ON:Warden|Warden]]{{Crown Store}} ![[ON:Necromancer|Necromancer]]{{ESO EL}} ![[ON:Arcanist|Arcanist]]{{ESO NE}} |- |[[ON:Ardent Flame|Ardent Flame]]

These lines are: {| | *[[ON:Two Handed|Two Handed]] *[[ON:One Hand and Shield|One Hand and Shield]] *[[ON:Dual Wield|Dual Wield]] | *[[ON:Bow|Bow]] *[[ON:Destruction Staff|Destruction Staff]] *[[ON:Restoration Staff|Restoration Staff]] |} Any class can advance in any of the Weapon skill lines by holding the appropriate weapon at the moment of gaining experience (whether that experience is gained by killing a monster, completing a quest or by any other means). Advancement will be faster by slotting one of the active weapon skills on your current skill bar (skills 1-5, or the Ultimate) when gaining experience points, with more slotted skills granting faster advancement. If you slot weapon skills for a weapon you are not holding (e.g. slot a dual-wield skill while holding a two-handed weapon), both the individual skills (from I to IV) and the overall weapon skill (from 1 to 50) will gain progress. ==Armor== There are three armor skill lines: *[[ON:Light_Armor|Light Armor]] *[[ON:Medium_Armor|Medium Armor]] *[[ON:Heavy_Armor|Heavy Armor]] Any class can advance in any of the Armor skill lines, while wearing the appropriate armor type. Only 1 piece need be worn, but progress will be faster the more pieces you wear of that type. ==Racial== Each [[ON:Races|race]] has its own skill line which becomes available at level 5. Your overall character level determines the abilities you may choose from your racial skills. See: {| | *[[ON:Argonian|Argonian]] *[[ON:Breton|Breton]] *[[ON:Dark Elf|Dark Elf]] *[[ON:High Elf|High Elf]] *[[ON:Imperial|Imperial]] | *[[ON:Khajiit|Khajiit]] *[[ON:Nord|Nord]] *[[ON:Orc|Orc]] *[[ON:Redguard|Redguard]] *[[ON:Wood Elf|Wood Elf]] |} Progress in the Racial skill lines is directly equivalent to your character's overall experience level. ==World== Not all of the skill lines are visible at the beginning of the game. You must discover other skill lines around the world, by completing certain quests, or finding certain items. The six World skill lines are: *[[ON:Excavation|Excavation]] {{ESO GM}} - obtained by the quest [[ON:The Antiquarian Circle (quest)|The Antiquarian Circle]] *[[ON:Legerdemain|Legerdemain]] - obtained by breaking the law *[[ON:Werewolf|Lycanthropy]] - obtained by becoming a werewolf *[[ON:Scrying|Scrying]] {{ESO GM}} - obtained by the quest [[ON:The Antiquarian Circle (quest)|The Antiquarian Circle]] *[[ON:Soul Magic|Soul Magic]] - obtained by progress through the main quest *[[ON:Vampire|Vampirism]] - obtained by becoming a vampire ==Guild== The Guild skill lines include lines for NPC guilds: *[[ON:Dark Brotherhood|Dark Brotherhood]]{{ESO DLC|Dark Brotherhood}} *[[ON:Fighters Guild|Fighters Guild]] *[[ON:Mages Guild|Mages Guild]] *[[ON:Psijic Order|Psijic Order]]{{ESO SS}} *[[ON:Thieves Guild|Thieves Guild]]{{ESO DLC|Thieves Guild}} *[[ON:Undaunted|Undaunted]] Progress in the Guild quest lines (usually from 1 to 10 - the Thieves and Dark Brotherhood go up to 12) is done by doing guild faction quests, both in the faction's quest storylines and other repeatable quests (usually daily) that are related to the faction. In most cases (except for the Psijic Order which consists only of the quest storyline), you will HAVE to do some of the repeatable stuff to level your faction reputation up high enough to continue the storyline, or to level it up to maximum after the storyline is completed, because the storyline itself does not give you enough progress to reach the next stage of the quest storyline. *Fighters Guild progress is gained by killing undeads, Daedra or werewolves anywhere, and by doing daily quests to clear Dark Anchors. *Mages Guild progress is gained by finding Lorebooks, and by doing daily quests involving finding relics in Public Dungeons. *Thieves Guild and Dark Brotherhood progress are made by doing repeatable quests (thefts or murders, respectively). Some of these quests are daily, others can be repeated as often as you like. *Psijic Order has no daily or otherwise repeatable quests, and progress is obtained only through the quest storyline. *Undaunted faction reputation is gained by clearing Dungeon quest storylines (once per dungeon), or by doing the daily Pledges from the three quest givers at the Undaunted Enclave, or by doing the daily solo delve quests given by Bolgrul at the enclave. The Undaunted have no overarching quest storyline. ==Alliance War== Alliance War skill lines are the Player vs Player lines. These include siege weapons and other PvP abilities. Currently there are three Alliance War skill lines in the game: *[[ON:Assault|Assault]] *[[ON:Support|Support]] *[[ON:Emperor|Emperor]] - a set of passive abilities possessed only by current Emperors Progress in the Assault and Support lines comes as you gain Alliance War points for any PVP or alliance-war related activities - killing other players (in Cyrodiil, Imperial City or Battlegrounds), completing daily quests in Cyrodiil (both the war quests, and the PVE quests in Cyrodiil's various towns), capturing or successfully defending keeps and resources, capturing Elder Scrolls, and competing in Battlegrounds. Even getting Alliance Points from daily rewards from your ESO+ subscription counts towards Assault/Support progress on whichever of your characters is used to claim the reward. You only need to reach about halfway from level 13 to 14 in Alliance War rank, to max out the Assault and Support lines at 10 each (they both increase together at the same rate). ===Artifacts=== In addition to the above, participating in the Alliance War has a chance to provide you with the use of certain unique [[ON:Artifacts|Artifacts]] that grant you special powers: *[[ON:Volendrung|Volendrung]] *[[ON:Auriel's Bow|Auriel's Bow]] ''(upcoming)'' *[[ON:Sanguine's Rose|Sanguine's Rose]] ''(upcoming)'' ==Craft== [[ON:Crafting|Crafting]] skill lines are each related to a profession and help boost the products you create in the related profession. These include: *[[ON:Alchemy|Alchemy]] - which allows you to craft custom potions *[[ON:Blacksmithing|Blacksmithing]] - allows you to craft custom melee weapons and heavy armor *[[ON:Clothing|Clothing]] - allows you to craft custom light and medium armor *[[ON:Enchanting|Enchanting]] - allows you to craft custom enchantments to apply to your gear *[[ON:Jewelry Crafting|Jewelry Crafting]]{{ESO SS}} - allows you to craft custom rings and necklaces *[[ON:Provisioning|Provisioning]] - allows you to craft custom food and beverages *[[ON:Woodworking|Woodworking]] - allows you to craft custom bows, staves, and shields In all seven cases, you learn by doing it, and by completing the daily crafting writs once you have been certified as a craftsman of that skill. In the case of Blacksmithing, Clothing, Enchanting, Jewelry Crafting and Woodworking, you learn even faster by deconstructing found items (although you gain almost no progress from deconstructing an item you made yourself - however, you get full progress from deconstructing items made by another character, even if that other character is one of your own on the same account). The higher the quality of item you deconstruct, the more "inspiration" is gained towards that craft, especially if the item in question has the "Intricate" trait. Alchemy and Provisioning have no Deconstruction, and Enchanting has no equivalent to the Intricate trait on worn/wielded equipment. ==Dungeon== These skills are temporarily available as part of Online:Emperor:
{{About|the skill line|the achievement and related title|Emperor!}} {{Trail2|Skill Lines|Alliance War}} [[File:ON-costume-Emperor's Regalia (Male).jpg|thumb|left|A character in Emperor's Regalia]]{{TOCright}} For each Campaign in the [[ON:Alliance War|Alliance War]], it is possible for a player to be selected as '''Emperor'''. There can only be one Emperor for each Campaign, though there may be multiple campaigns, and thus multiple Emperors. In order to be crowned Emperor, your [[ON:Alliances|Alliance]] must control all six of the [[ON:Keeps|Keeps]] surrounding the Imperial City ([[ON:Chalman Keep|Chalman Keep]], [[ON:Blue Road Keep|Blue Road Keep]], [[ON:Castle Alessia|Castle Alessia]], [[ON:Castle Roebeck|Castle Roebeck]], [[ON:Fort Ash|Fort Ash]] and [[ON:Fort Aleswell|Fort Aleswell]]) and you must be the highest-ranked player in your Alliance. Your ranking is affected by the number of [[ON:Alliance Points|Alliance Points]] you have, which can be earned by participating in PvP battles. Your crown will be forfeit if your Alliance loses control of all six surrounding Keeps or if you leave the Campaign for another. By becoming Emperor, you also gain a unique [[Online:Emperor's Regalia|costume]] and the "Emperor" and "Empress" title. After being deposed, your title will change to "Former Emperor" and "Former Empress" but you will still have access to the costume. Emperors cannot wield [[Online:Volendrung|Volendrung]] for balance reasons. {{FMI|Battlefield Emperors}} {{NewLine}} ==Skill Perks== As Emperor, you gain access to several innate Passive abilities. '''Augur''' allows you to detect the relative (or, in some cases, absolute) location of an [[ON:Antiquities|Antiquity]]. It can only be used on dirt less than four layers deep— the area underneath it will flash red if it cannot be used. Its upgrade will allow you to use it over dirt that is less than seven layers deep. Augur does not consume any time, but it has a limited number of uses{{huh|how many?}} before it stops working.
[[File:ON-activity-Excavation Interface 03.PNG|An illustration of the different colors and their respective range|thumb|left]]
The distance is color-designated: if you are on top of the Antiquity, it will glow green, but if you are more than 5 squares away from it, it will turn red. Note that it only detects Antiquities, not bonus loot. Below are the colors relative to the Augur's distance from the Antiquity.
* '''Red''' — A faint red outline with no glow. The antiquity is at least 5 squares away from the selected square.
* '''Orange''' — An orange outline with a slight glow. The antiquity is 3-4 squares away from the selected square.
* '''Yellow''' — A yellow outline with a strong glow.  The antiquity is 1-2 squares away from the selected square.
* '''Green''' — A bright green outline with a pulsating, strong glow. The antiquity is directly beneath the selected square.

It is immediately unlocked upon completion of [[ON:The Antiquarian Circle (quest)|The Antiquarian Circle quest]].

Online:Banner Bearer:
{{Trail|Scribing}}
[[File:ON-icon-book-grimoire-Support.png|right]]
:''Bring out a banner to inspire yourself and nearby group members.''

'''Banner Bearer''' is a [[ON:Scribing|Scribed]] skill [[ON:Scribing#Grimoires|Grimoire]] on the [[ON:Support|Support]] skill line.  It can be purchased after earning the [[ON:Alliance War Skill Apprentice|Alliance War Skill Apprentice]] achievement from [[ON:Chronicler Firandil|Chronicler Firandil]] in [[ON:The Scholarium|the Scholarium]] once per character.  Note that unlike all the other Grimoires, you must earn the associated achievement individually on each character in order to purchase it, while for the others you only need the achievement on the first character.
It costs {{ESO Price|50,000}} the first time, and {{ESO Price|10,000}} for other characters on your account after that.

Banner Bearer causes you to bring out a banner, which will be attached to your back. The skill costs a constant amount of {{ESO Magicka Link}} and {{ESO Stamina Link}} every two seconds ({{ESO Health Link}} and {{ESO Stamina Link}} with Immobilize Focus Script).  While active, you and any group members near you will gain certain buffs, depending on your choice of scripts.  The banner remains active indefinitely until you put it away by casting the skill again, swapping skill bars (unless you have the skill on both bars), running out of one of the two required resources, or changing zones.

*Cast Time: Instant
*Radius: 8 meters

'''Blade of Woe''' lets you instantly kill NPC targets, provided you approach them while in stealth from behind. You only receive one quarter of the experience from such kills, meaning that it is primarily useful for avoiding a bounty when attacking [[Online:Reaction|innocent]] NPCs. You cannot use it on other players or bosses.

You receive this skill for free during the quest [[Online:Voices in the Dark|Voices in the Dark]] as part of the [[Online:Dark Brotherhood (DLC)|Dark Brotherhood DLC]]. It functions as a [[Online:Synergy|synergy]].

This skill can be buffed significantly by slotting the [[Online:Shadowstrike|Shadowstrike]] Champion Point perk.
{{NewLeft}}
==[[Online:Tutorials|Tutorials]] Description==
''Members of the Dark Brotherhood can call upon the Blade of Woe, an artifact with the power to instantly slay unaware targets.''

''To use the Blade of Woe, position yourself behind your target while hidden. If that target is vulnerable to the Blade of Woe, you will be prompted to press [MB4] to trigger the assassination. This is similar to the way you would activate a Synergy.''

''Killing a target with the Blade of Woe has a chance to grant you Dried Blood or Tainted Blood, which can be used to craft gear in the Assassins League style.''

''The Blade of Woe can only be used on humanoids, cannot be used in Group Dungeons or in Trials, and cannot be used against certain powerful enemies.''

''Using the Blade of Woe does not prevent you from being witnessed by bystanders, so keep an eye on your surroundings!''


== Notes ==
*The [[Lore:Blade of Woe|Blade of Woe]] also appeared in both ''[[Oblivion:Blade of Woe|Oblivion]]'' and ''[[Skyrim:Blade of Woe|Skyrim]]''
*The Blade of Woe deals 100% of the target's {{ESO Health Link|Max}} in [[ON:Oblivion Damage|oblivion damage]].
*The Blade of Woe takes precedence over feeding as a [[Online:Vampire|vampire]] in close range. To feed after acquiring this skill, you must be slightly further away from your target.
*Blade of Woe does not work on all humanoid NPC targets. For example, it will work on [[Online:Breton|Bretons]] or [[Online:Dremora|Dremora]], but not on [[Online:Goblin|goblins]]. As such, it is most effective against heavily resistant opponents. '''Boneyard''' deals [[ON:Frost Damage|Frost Damage]] to all enemies within a selected area.  If there is a corpse in the area to consume, the damage is increased.  Allies may activate the {{ESO Synergy Link|Grave Robber}} Synergy to deal additional damage and also restore their {{ESO Health Link}}.  The '''Unnerving Boneyard''' morph reduces the resistances of all affected enemies as well as making them more vulnerable to further damage, while '''Avid Boneyard''' allows you to activate the Synergy yourself.

== Patch Notes ==
{{ESO Patch Note|7.3.5|* This ability and its morphs now grant a stack of up to 30 Weapon and Spell Damage rather than 600 upfront, up to a maximum of 10 stacks.
* Decreased the tick frequency to 2 seconds, down from 1 (haha inverse math!) so the ability drains Health slower.
* The health cost now increases by 250 Health per stack, rather than 20% of the cost of the skill with no cap.
* Reduced the initial cost to 700, down from 1980.
** Simmering Frenzy (morph): This morph now increases the Weapon and Spell Damage granted to a maximum of 40 per stack, rather than adding 66 Weapon and Spell Damage each second the ability is toggled on with no cap.
** Sated Frenzy (morph): This morph now also reduces the ramping cost of the ability to 200 per stack, down from 250.
**''Developer Comment: This ability and its morphs are currently enabling incredibly polarizing gameplay; it feeds into an intense risk/reward mechanic that can often be mitigated heavily by specialized classes and builds that stack life steal, paired with deep knowledge of content and combat interactions. In its current form, it feels too penalizing for the base Vampire experience to engage with in a satisfying way while also enabling an overwhelming amount of power for those who know how to use it properly. This iteration now significantly reduces both the penalty and the bonus of the effect to make it more accessible and balanced overall, helping it feel more like a Damage over Time alternative where an ability can be active for prolonged periods of time with slightly more risk/reward than usual.''}}
{{ESO Patch Note|8.0.5|* This ability and its morphs now grant up to 5 stacks, rather than 10. The total Weapon and Spell Damage granted is left untouched.
* The cost now increases by 360 per tick, up from 250, for Blood and Simmering Frenzy, while the cost for Sated Frenzy is now 300, rather than 200. This will result in an approximate 20% cost reduction for each morph.
**''Developer Comment: Based on much of the initial feedback we saw over last update, we've decided to help this ability ramp up a little quicker to make it feel more aggressive and ravenous for the user, while slightly easing back on the risk of using it since the reward isn't nearly as high as before.''}}

As this passive does not bring any facets into your area of control, it can be used anywhere, and does not need to envelop a full 6 facets to work. '''Dragon Leap''' deals physical damage to all enemies in the area around your target, and [[ON:Knockback|knocks them back]].  It is very effective at disabling a crowd for a short time.  The '''Take Flight''' morph increases its range and damage, and reduces the cost, so it can be used more frequently.  Or you can use the '''Ferocious Leap''' to give yourself some protection in the form of a [[ON:Damage Shield|Damage Shield]] after your leap, while also dealing [[Online:Fire Damage|Flame Damage]].
{{Newleft}}
==Notes==
* Dragon Leap and its morphs all apply a 0.25 second long 75% snare to the initial target when cast. This snare bypasses the crowd control immunity and Flying immunities enemies can have. This has been put in place as a band-aid to desynchronizations and lags that caused Dragon Leap and its morphs to often miss their initial target.
* This is similar in both cost and effect to the [[ON:Fighters Guild|Fighters Guild]] ultimate [[ON:Dawnbreaker|Dawnbreaker of Smiting]], though Dragon Leap deals comparatively more damage and can be used to close the distance to an enemy.
* Take Flight is a recommended morph for the [[ON:Venomous Dragon|Venomous Dragon]] build.

<section begin="description" />
'''Dilation''' allows you to claim facets that share the same type as a facet contiguous to your area of control. Unlike Scry, it does not claim ''all'' contiguous facets of the same type, unless it is upgraded.

Dilation's upgrade more or less combines the power of Scry to it, where it will catch ''all'' contiguous facets of the same type if it touches the targeted area of control.

'''Finders Keepers''' lets you open and loot [[ON:Thieves Trove|Thieves Troves]], found all over Tamriel. You receive the skill for free the first time you find one of these troves, which can only be opened when you have access to the [[ON:Thieves Guild (DLC)|Thieves Guild DLC]]. Alternatively, you'll acquire the skill during the quest [[ON:Partners in Crime|Partners in Crime]] if you haven't found a trove by then.

These troves have a distinctive blue glow, and produce an audible hum when you are near them, much like [[ON:Nirnroot|Nirnroot]] plants. Looting a trove is considered a crime, so be sure you are not witnessed opening it. Additionally, all of the contents will be marked as stolen, and will be confiscated if you are captured by the guards.

==Notes==
* In effect, acquiring this skill does nothing other than allow you to continue to open Thieves Troves even if your [[ON:ESO Plus|ESO Plus]] membership runs out and you lose access to the DLC.
* Thieves Troves are one of the easiest ways to find items in the [[ON:Night Mother's Embrace|Night Mother's Embrace]] set.

'''Feral Guardian''' summons a bear to fight for you that deals [[ON:Magic Damage|Magic Damage]] over time and occasionally deals Area Effect damage in front of it, stunning enemies hit.  Summoning the bear has no cost, but once summoned, you can activate '''Guardian's Wrath''' for {{ESO Ultimate Link|75}} which causes [[ON:Magic Damage|Magic Damage]] and deals 100% additional damage to targets under 25% health. The '''Eternal Guardian''' morph will respawn when killed (once per minute) so you don't need to worry about re-summoning it each time and increases the damage of Guardian's Wrath to low Health targets, while '''Wild Guardian''' deals [[ON:Bleed Damage|Bleed Damage]] instead and quintuples the chance of applying the Hemorrhaging status effect.

{{NewLeft}}
==Notes==
* Players who purchase the [[ON:Morrowind|Morrowind]] [[ON:Morrowind Collector's Edition|Collectors Edition]] or Collectors Pack upgrade are granted access to the {{Item Link|collectid=1260|Slate-Gray Summoned Bear}}, a unique gray skin for the bear which can be equipped through the [[ON:Collections|Collections]] menu.
* While summoning the bear can be done at any time (and should be done well in advance of battle given its long casting time), using its special ability requires a target, which the bear will rush and attack immediately.  In solo PvE play against tougher opponents, this is most effective as an opening attack, as NPCs tend to concentrate their attacks on whoever attacks them first, so by opening with this ability and standing back for a few seconds, you can let the bear take the brunt of the attacks.
*Feral Guardian will be unsummoned if you use your weapon swap unless you have selected the skill as your ultimate on both bars.  If you have the [[ON:Bond With Nature|Bond With Nature]] passive, this can be used to quickly restore some {{ESO Health Link}} at no cost, but given the casting time of re-summoning the bear when you switch back (even though this is also free), this is not a particularly viable strategy.
* Eternal Guardian is a recommended morph for the [[ON:Warden Initiate|Warden Initiate]] build.
* This skill was called "War Bear" in pre-release material.

'''Farsight''' allows you to claim up to four facets in a line, from a facet contiguous to a facet of your control. This can be done in any direction, and you do not need to select four facets in order to use it (which means a misclick can waste it). You can touch the area of your control from the side, but it will not allow you to select unless the starting facet is within a hexagon of your area of control.

Farsight's upgrade increases the number of facets you can select to 6.

It costs resources for as long as you hold the beam but you can stop this attack at any moment. Fatecarver also consumes your Crux to increase its damage. The '''Exhausting Fatecarver''' morph adds a snare and consuming Crux will also increase the snare's potency and the whole skill length. The '''Pragmatic Fatecarver''' morph gives you a large damage shield which also grants crowd control immunity for as long as you channel this skill and it isn't depleted. Consuming Crux will also reduce the skill's cost.
{{Newleft}}
==Notes==
* The cost and the damage are listed as ''per 0.3 seconds'' while in reality it is per 0.338 seconds.
* Fatecarver does not deal damage for the first 0.5 seconds of the channel.
* It is currently the only skill in the game that casts on button press instead of button release.

'''Frozen Gate''' creates a trap on the ground that will teleport an enemy directly to you and [[ON:Immobilize|Immobilize]] them for a short time.  The target will still be able to attack, but not move.  You may have up to three portals at a time.  The '''Frozen Device''' morph which reduces all damage dealt by the affected target.  Alternatively, you can choose '''Frozen Retreat''', which will allow your allies to use the portal as well via the {{ESO Synergy Link|Icy Escape}} synergy.  In either case, the portal disappears after a single use.

==Notes==
* Only one enemy is affected even if multiple enemies are inside the gate when it activates.
* The gate is not visible to the enemy except as a brief cloud of mist when the gate arms.
* There must be a clear path between you and the enemy and a place for the enemy to land for the teleport to work.  The immobilization will still take effect.
* Can be used alongside [[ON:Nature's Grasp|Nature's Grasp]] to both teleport an enemy to your location and then quickly jump to an ally's location, leaving the target stuck in place with nobody to attack.
* This skill is a good way of breaking up groups of enemies, as the target's allies may not immediately attack, or they may take a while getting to you, so it's best to use this on ranged attackers such as spellcasters or archers, as melee attackers are likely to approach you anyhow once they notice you.  This can be a useful tool as an alternative to [[ON:Taunt|Taunt]]ing for a tank build, especially with the '''Frozen Device''' morph.
* The '''Frozen Retreat''' morph is more useful for healers, to keep allies in the same area so that they are easier to cast healing and buffs on.  
* The rune placed uses [[Lore:Runic Alphabet|alphabet]] seen on [[Online:Runestones|runestones]], displaying (in clockwise order) Jayde and Rakeipa in the top right, Makko and Deikepa at the bottom, and Odra and Okoma in the top left.

|linerank1=4

}}
<section begin="description" />
The '''Heavy Shovel''' is a tool used when excavating an antiquity that digs up 1 layer of dirt in a 3x3 area. It can only be used once you have at least 2 intuition (which is generated from using the [[ON:Hand Brush|Hand Brush]] two times). It is most useful when you have already located the exact or approximate location of the antiquity using the [[ON:Augur|Augur]] skill, as it allows you to clear large patches of dirt in one go. Note that if the 3x3 area contains dirt at different layers, only the dirt at the center tile ''and dirt directly connected to the center tile at the same height'' will be dug up. Therefore, for efficient use, it is recommended to first ensure all dirt in the 3x3 area is at the same height using the Hand Brush tool.

Upon unlocking the second upgrade, the Heavy Shovel will occasionally not consume any Intuition. This allows it to be used several times in a row, therefore greatly shortening the time taken to excavate an antiquity and allowing more time to search for bonus loot.

If you have the second Hand Brush upgrade, it is possible to store up to 4 intuition and therefore use the Heavy Shovel to dig two layers down in one go. It thus becomes important to check that you are not already digging up the lowest layer, otherwise you will damage the antiquity. Higher level antiquities are especially delicate and can be damaged in one hit.
<section end="description" />

'''Gnash''' deals [[ON:Physical Damage|Physical Damage]] to a single target on the initial attack, and additional [[ON:Bleed Damage|Bleed Damage]]. The attack will consume a stack of Blood Hunger (which is generated by other Werewolf active abilities) and increase the initial damage caused. The second hit will cause increased damage to targets with less than {{ESO Health Link|25%}}.

The '''Rip and Tear''' morph will apply [[ON:Sundered|Sundered]] and [[Online:Major Breach|Major Breach]] on the initial hit and Bleed Damage afterward. The second hit will also heal you if it connects, depending on your {{ESO Health Link|Max}}. The second hit will cause increased damage to targets with less than {{ESO Health Link|25%}}. Additionally, the consumed Blood Hunger stack will increase healing rather than damage.

The '''Bloody Gnash''' morph and will apply Blood Hunger to increase damage on the first hit, and has a 50% chance of retaining the Blood Hunger stack. The morph will always apply Hemorrhaging on the second hit and increases the execute scaling on this attack for enemies with less than {{ESO Health Link|25%}}.

==Patch Notes==
{{ESO Patch Note|12.0.5|*Piercing Howl -> Gnash: This ability and its morphs have been completely reworked into a melee (7m) driven double bite attack, rather than a 10m projectile howl attack. The ability now scales with .525 of your Weapon or Spell Damage and .065 of your Magicka or Stamina twice, rather than a singular 1.3125 and .125 scaling attack. The initial hit deals Physical Damage, while the second hit deals Bleed Damage. Both attacks have a 10% chance of applying their respective status effects. The second hit happens after .4s (no cast time, so it can be animation canceled with no loss) and deals 125% bonus damage to targets under 25% Health. If 1 or more stacks of Blood Hunger are active, the initial hit deals 25% bonus damage and 1 stack is consumed. Reduced the cost of this ability and its morphs to 765, down from 2869.
**Howl of Agony -> Bloody Gnash: This morph now adds a 50% chance when benefiting from Blood Hunger to not consume a stack. This morph also upgrades the 2nd hit to always apply the Hemorrhaging status effect. Increased the execute scaling of the 2nd hit to 200%. This morph no longer increases damage done against Off Balance targets or reduces in cost as it ranks up.
**Howl of Despair -> Rip and Tear: This morph upgrades the 1st hit to always apply the Sundered status effect, as well as inflicting Major Breach to the target for 12-15 seconds. The second hit heals you for .2066 of your Max Health (and ranks up by 1.1% per rank) if it hits. Blood Hunger’s 25% increase applies to the healing effect for this morph, rather than the base damage. This morph no longer grants access to Feeding Frenzy, as it has been moved to Roar.
{{Showhide/Start|Developer Comment}}
''Werewolves have finally learned to put their jaws to use with this new spammable, rending flesh from their foes with a much more brutal two part attack – gone are the days of angrily yelling your opponents to death. Gnash operates as both your standard fare single target spammable and an execute both in one, helping make up for the Werewolf’s bar space deficit while leaning into their fantasy of masters of the hunt. A hunter who cannot finish off their prey often returns empty handed after all. This helps Werewolves become significantly more terrifying to low health foes, while giving them reason to stick closer to their enemies and make use of their speed boosts in melee range. The morphs once again split with more diversity, granting two utility driven effects that can both lead to more damage, but with more of an option between damage or survivability. The previous iteration of "terrified" has also been reworked to Blood Hunger, which has slightly more interaction across their kit, while also being easier to use.''
{{Showhide/End}}}}

'''Kickback''' reduces the penalties you must pay to guards or fences if you are caught committing a crime. Though you could just escape and stay away from towns or cities until your bounty goes away on its own, a very large bounty can take a long time to clear. This can bring the payable total down to manageable levels that can be offset by fencing some fine or better quality contraband. 

Note that this does not reduce the amount of bounty actually incurred by a crime, it merely reduces the amount of gold paid to guards or fences to clear your bounty. (Ex. Committing a minor crime that gives 92 bounty will still incur 92 bounty with Kickback I, it just reduces the amount paid to the guard/fence to 83.) This skill has no interaction with bounty decay, whether natural or enhanced by Swiftly Forgotten.

'''Mend Wounds''' this is a toggle ability that replaces your Light and Heavy attacks with healing spells that can be used on an ally.  After casting, your [[ON:Light Attack|Light Attack]] will heal for a small amount, or by a larger amount for as long as you channel a [[ON:Heavy Attack|Heavy Attack]] that also returns magicka.  The '''Mend Spirit''' morph will also increase your target's resistances while healing, while '''Symbiosis''' heals you as well by half of the amount of your ally. '''Mender's Bond''' is a [[ON:Scribing|Scribed]] skill [[ON:Scribing#Grimoires|Grimoire]] on the [[ON:Restoration Staff|Restoration Staff]] skill line.  It can be purchased after earning the [[ON:Restoration Staff Master|Restoration Staff Master]] achievement from [[ON:Chronicler Firandil|Chronicler Firandil]] in [[ON:The Scholarium|the Scholarium]] once per character. 
It costs {{ESO Price|50,000}} the first time, and {{ESO Price|10,000}} for other characters on your account after that.  Prior to [[ON:Update 44|Update 44]], this grimoire was unique in that it was the only one whose name does not change based on your choice of Focus Script.  It was always just "Mender's Bond".

Mender's Bond creates a tether between you and a target.  The target of Mender's Bond can be any ally, whether another player, a [[ON:Companions|companion]], or many friendly NPCs.  (The only exception to this seems to be that the Mitigation Focus script can target other players or companions, but ''not'' other NPCs.)  Depending on your choice of scripts, either allies or enemies (possibly both) standing between you and the target, "in the link" as the descriptions say, will be affected in some way.

*Range: 20 meters
*Duration: 12 seconds
*Cost: {{ESO Magicka Link|3969}}

'''Overload''' applies [[Online:Shock Damage|Shock Damage]] to all standard light and heavy attacks for the duration of the effect.  The light attack affects a single target (at a range, regardless of your equipped weapon), while a heavy attack hits all enemies in front of you.  The heavy attack can be held down for a continuous attack until you run out of {{ESO Ultimate Link}}.  '''Power Overload''' increases the attack range and damage done, while '''Energy Overload''' restores {{ESO Magicka Link}} and {{ESO Stamina Link}} with each attack.
{{Newleft}}
==Notes==
* This ability was reworked in [[ON:Update 20|Update 20]].  Prior to this update:
** When activating Overload, you would gain an additional skill bar that can only be modified while Overload was active.  You could use any skills except for weapon skills on this bar.  Note that just like your weapon-swap bar, any toggle-type skills (such as summons) had to be in the same slot on both your normal and Overload skill bars, or they would be canceled when you switched between normal and Overload mode.
** You could not use your weapon-swap while Overload was active.  Any passive bonuses from your equipped weapon would also be disabled.  Set bonuses from weapons and/or shield would still apply, however.
* Unlike other {{ESO Ultimate Link}} abilities, Overload does not fully empty your {{ESO Ultimate Link}} pool, it only subtracts a small amount of {{ESO Ultimate Link}} for each light attack, or drains slowly over time while performing a heavy attack.
* The heavy attack does direct damage and hits every 1 second.

'''See the Unseen''' allows you to see and interact with [[ON:Psijic Portals|Psijic Portals]] all around Tamriel. You will receive this skill for free immediately upon acquiring the Psijic Order skill line by completing the first quest, [[ON:The Psijics' Calling|The Psijics' Calling]].

==Loot==
These portals may contain a variety of valuable loot, including:

* Chapters from [[ON:Crafting Motifs|crafting motif]] books associated with the zone the portal was found in (e.g. Sapiarch motifs in Summerset).
* Armor or weapon [[ON:Overland Sets|Overland Set]] pieces associated with the zone the portal was found in.
* Jewelry with the [[ON:Infused|Infused]] trait for research as well as the {{Item Link|Aurbic Amber|id=139411}} material for that trait (in refined or, more commonly, {{Item Link|pulverized|id=139417}} form)
* [[Online:Runestones|Runestones]] and other assorted crafting materials, including {{Item Link|id=68342|Hakeijo}} rune with a very low chance.  
* Very rarely a {{Item Link|Psijic Ambrosia|quality=5|id=64221}} consumable.
* {{Item Link|Lead: Sticky Integument Leather|quality=5|antiquityid=114}} [[ON:Antiquities|antiquity lead]] for the [[Online:Thrassian Stranglers|Thrassian Stranglers]] ([[ON:Summerset|Summerset]] and [[ON:Artaeum|Artaeum]] only).
* {{Item Link|Lead: Beacon of Tower Zero|quality=5|antiquityid=281}} [[ON:Antiquities|antiquity lead]] for the [[Online:Beacon of Tower Zero|Beacon of Tower Zero]] [[Online:Antiquity_Furnishings|antiquity furnishing]] ([[ON:Stormhaven|Stormhaven]] only).
* {{Item Link|Lead: Dov-rha Sabaton Toe Cap|quality=5|antiquityid=460}} [[ON:Antiquities|antiquity lead]] for the [[Online:Dov-rha Sabatons|Dov-rha Sabatons]] ([[ON:Southern Elsweyr|Southern Elsweyr]] only).

==Notes==
*Psijic Portals appear in the same locations where Runestone [[ON:nodes|nodes]] are typically found, near old ruins and burial sites.  Similar to Runestone nodes, they will always contain one Runestone of each type, Aspect, Essence, and Potency, but the Aspect rune will always be {{ESO Rune Link|Jejota}} or better.
*This is similar in many respects to the [[ON:Thieves Guild|Thieves Guild]] skill [[ON:Finders Keepers|Finders Keepers]].  It differs in that unlike Thieves Troves, Psijic Portals are not even visible to those without the skill, and also interacting with them is not a crime.

{{ESO Patch Note|3.0.5|* This ability now causes your Light and Heavy Attacks to restore Health instead of Magicka or Stamina.
* Increased the duration of this ability and its morphs to 20 seconds from 15 seconds.
* Reduced the cost of this ability and its morphs by approximately 50%.
* Recasting this ability or its morphs early will now always trigger the ending resource restore. The value of this restore is based on the length of time the abilities were active, similar to Rally's heal.
* Each Light or Heavy Attack from this ability or its morphs will now restore less resources, but the final burst at the end will restore more resources. The total resources restored by this ability will remain roughly the same.
* Leeching Strikes: This morph now converts the ability into a Stamina ability and causes your Light and Heavy Attacks to restore Stamina based on your character level, and an additional burst of Stamina when the effect ends.

The changes also make the resource restore portion of these abilities better if you are not weaving Light Attacks perfectly, which is desirable for tanks and healers who spend time blocking or healing.''}}
{{ESO Patch Note|3.0.7|* Leeching Strikes: Fixed an issue where Rank III of this morph was not returning the correct amount of Stamina when the ability ended.}}
{{ESO Patch Note|3.0.9|* Leeching Strikes: Fixed an issue where you could block the heal from this morph.}}
{{ESO Patch Note|4.0.5|* Leeching Strikes: Fixed an issue where this morph was unable to be cast while you were silenced.}}
{{ESO Patch Note|4.2.5|* Fully charged Heavy Attacks now restore twice the amount of Health and resources for this ability and its morphs.}}
{{ESO Patch Note|4.3.5|* The heal from Siphoning Strikes and Morphs will no longer be considered "proc" abilities, meaning it can proc other proc abilities such as item sets and enchants.
** Note: We will continue evaluating which abilities should and should not be considered procs in the future.}}
{{ESO Patch Note|5.0.5|* Fixed an issue where this ability and its morphs had a cooldown on the heal. Since Light and Heavy Attacks already have their own unique cooldowns, this previous interaction meant if you had a set such as Blood Moon, you were not gaining the full efficiency of the bonus.}}
{{ESO Patch Note|6.0.5|* Fixed an issue where this ability and its morphs could proc off Mend Wounds and its morphs. The soul-stealing power of this ability is now reserved for damaging Light and Heavy Attacks.}}
{{ESO Patch Note|9.3.5|* Reworked this ability and its morphs to be simpler to use, while making their resource recovery more engaging.
* When activated, the ability will instantly drain 4000 Health to restore 2000 Magicka and Stamina.
* When the ability is slotted on either bar, any damage you deal will heal you for 1250 Health, up to once every second.
** Leeching Strikes (morph): This morph now increases the passive healing done to 1800 Health. Whenever the heal activates, it reduces the cost of your next Leeching Strikes cast by 10%, stacking up to 10 times. The cost reduction lasts until consumed, your character dies, or you rezone.
** Siphoning Attacks (morph): This morph now increases the resources restored to 2600 Magicka and Stamina. Whenever the heal activates, it also restores 200 Magicka and Stamina.
*** ''Developer Comment:The Nightblade class has long been limited in its overall performance by how well the player can utilize Light and Heavy Attacks between each ability, making it very difficult for many players and build types. In efforts to ease back some of this demand, we’re moving forward with a rework to their primary sustain tool to be more usable by any build or player. Rather than needing to constantly activate the ability to be eligible to heal when you properly weave, it now passively heals you anytime you deal damage, simply for having it slotted. The resource portion of the ability is now granted at the base level of the skill (rather than morphs) and no longer grants exclusive resources, but comes at a risky cost of Health – which we hope the passive healing helps lessen the risk of engaging with. Additionally, the morphs now focus on the different aspects of the skill, where Leeching Strikes focuses on raw healing and reducing the risk of activation, while Siphoning Attacks doubles down on resource recovery by adding a passive recovery option and increasing the rewards of its activation.''}}

'''Shocking Siphon''' consumes a corpse to deal [[ON:Shock Damage|Shock Damage]] to all enemies near the corpse or between you and the corpse.  The bond is broken if you move too far from the corpse or are physically blocked by walls or other static obstacles.  It also increases your damage done while slotted.  With the '''Detonating Siphon''' morph, the damage changes to [[ON:Disease Damage|Disease Damage]], and the corpse will explode at the end of the siphoning, dealing additional damage.  Alternatively, the '''Shocking Siphon''' morph restores your {{ESO Health Link}}, {{ESO Magicka Link}}, and {{ESO Stamina Link}} while the bond is active.

{{NewLeft}}
== Notes ==
* Detonating Siphon is a recommended morph for the [[ON:Deathbringer|Deathbringer]] build, while Mystic Siphon is recommended for [[ON:Necromancer Initiate|Necromancer Initiate]] and [[ON:Baleful Summoner|Baleful Summoner]].
* The Detonating Siphons corpse explode effect occurs even if you recast the ability early.
* Tethers are considered [[ON:Area of Effect|Area of Effect]] damage and are reduced by [[ON:Major Evasion|Major]]/[[ON:Minor Evasion|Minor Evasion]].

'''Shield Throw''' is a Scribed skill Grimoire, on the [[ON:One Hand and Shield|One Hand and Shield]] skill line.  It can be purchased after earning the [[ON:One Hand and Shield Master|One Hand and Shield Master]] achievement from [[ON:Chronicler Firandil|Chronicler Firandil]] in [[ON:The Scholarium|the Scholarium]] once per character.

It costs {{ESO Price|50,000}} the first time, and {{ESO Price|10,000}} for other characters on your account after that.  The name of the scribed skill changes depending upon your choice of Focus Script.

As the name implies, this skill causes you to throw your shield at an enemy target.  It will then bounce back to you, possibly having some effect both when it hits the enemy and when it returns, based on your choice of scripts.  The visuals for this skill unfortunately do not reflect your choice of [[ON:Crafting Motifs|Crafting Motifs]] for your shield - it just looks like a glowing circle (color dependent on Focus) regardless of your gear.

'''Summon Unstable Familiar''' summons an [[ON:Unstable Familiar|Unstable Familiar]] [[Online:Scamp|Scamp]] to aid you in battle. The familiar remains until killed or unsummoned. Casting the spell again while the familiar is alive causes the Scamp's attacks to deal additional pulses of [[ON:Shock Damage|Shock Damage]]. '''Summon Unstable Clannfear''' changes the summon to an [[ON:Unstable Clannfear|Unstable Clannfear]] instead, whose activation ability [[ON:Healing|heals]] both itself and you. The [[Online:Volatile Familiar|Volatile Familiar]] created with the '''Summon Volatile Familiar''' does more damage, and when cast again deals Shock Damage to all nearby enemies several times, with the second pulse of damage [[ON:Stun|stunning]] them.

==Notes==
*Previously, casting the spell with a familiar active would cause them to be unsummoned rather than using a special ability. To unsummon now, you must either right-click the corresponding active effect on your character page, or remove the skill from your skill bar (at least temporarily). This can be done with a weapon swap if you don't have the skill in the same slot on both weapon tabs. (Conversely, if you don't ''want'' the familiar to go away when you switch weapons, then you ''must'' have the skill on both tabs.)

Online:Synergy:
{{Trail|Combat/Skills}} '''Synergies''' are special abilities that other allied players may activate when you use certain skills or sets. If a Synergy is available to you, a prompt at the bottom of the screen appears letting you know that you can activate a Synergy, by pressing the key or buttons associated with it. ("'''X'''" by default on PC/Mac, [[File:UESP-icon-XB1 Y.png|20px|Y]]+[[File:UESP-icon-XB1 B.png|20px|B]] on Xbox, [[File:UESP-icon-PS4 Triangle.png|20px|Triangle]]+[[File:UESP-icon-PS4 Circle.png|20px|Circle]] on PS4). Synergy activations cost no resources and are independent of skill cooldowns. The [[ON:Undaunted|Undaunted]] skill line is particularly based on Synergies, as all of its active skills have one associated with them. Some Synergies only appear with certain skill morphs, or change depending on the morph chosen. Synergies are a great way of restoring resources through [[Online:Undaunted Command|Undaunted Command]], the [[Online:Harmony|Harmony]] jewelry trait, or the synergies' effect ===Cooldown=== Synergies have a 20 second cooldown per player for each individual Synergy. A single player can use several different synergies in quick succession, but must wait 20 seconds before using the same skills synergy again. Likewise if a synergy has multiple uses, a different player activating it has no effect on your cooldown or ability to activate it. All skill morphs synergies share a cooldown, so casting {{ESO Synergy Link|Combustion|nolink=y}} would place you on cooldown for using {{ESO Synergy Link|Healing Combustion|nolink=y}} Uniquely [[Online:Spear_Shards|Spear Shards]] and [[Online:Necrotic_Orb|Necrotic Orb]]'s synergies also share the same cooldown. Using one will prevent you from using the other for 20 seconds. ===Mechanics=== All synergies have a set amount of uses per cast of the skill. This is typically either 1, 3 or 12 uses. Recasting a skill will refresh that synergy's availability for the group. Most synergies can only be activated by group members, but there are some exceptions in the table below marked with {{intnote|special}} The activation range for each synergy is usually the spell's [[Online:Area of Effect|Area of Effect]], but can also be centered around a target or ally. From Patch 6.0.0 Synergies now have a hierarchy to determine which synergy appears first when multiple are present to you. Quest, Dungeon, Arena, and Trial-related synergies now always appear over player-sourced synergies. Furthermore, for player-sourced synergies, the following ruleset is applied: Healing and Shield-related synergies will take utmost priority. Utility, Buff, and Debuff synergies will appear next. Strictly Damage-related synergies are last in priority. {{Incomplete}}{{Trail|Skills}}[[File:ON-render-Subclassing.jpg|thumb|left|Subclassing Sorcerer-Dragonknight]][[File:ON-mapicon-Subclassing.png|right]] '''Subclassing''' is a system that was released in the base game [[Online:Update 46|Update 46]]. It allows a player to customize their character by replacing up to two of their [[Online:classes|class']] [[ON:Skills|skill lines]] with those from other classes. In order to use subclassing, you must first have at least one level 50 character; once this criterion is met, the quest [[ON:A Study in Discipline|A Study in Discipline]] must be completed on each character whose base class skill lines you wish to change. While base class skill lines are levelled separately on individual characters, progress in sub-classed skill lines is shared across all characters on your account. You can have up to three unlevelled sub-class skill lines at a time; once a subclass skill has been fully levelled, it is considered 'mastered' in the same way that base class skills can be mastered. A subclassed skill line gains access to all skills and passives in the same way as base class skill lines, although each stage costs two skill points instead of one. {{NewLeft}} ==How to Start== {{Incomplete|Needs mechanics etc}} [[File:ON-render-Bahtra at-Hunding.jpg|thumb|right|Meet Bahtra at-Hunding]] You will need at least one character at level 50, and then you can start the quest [[ON:A Study in Discipline|A Study in Discipline]] from the [[ON:Crown Store|Crown Store]] (at no cost). <section begin="description" />
The '''Trowel''' is a tool that digs up 3 layers of dirt in an excavation. It can only be used once you have at least 2 intuition (which is generated from using the [[ON:Hand Brush|Hand Brush]] two times). Care should be taken when using the Trowel since it is possible to damage the antiquity by digging too far down.

Upon unlocking the second upgrade, the Trowel can be used to trigger a detonation. This requires that you form a path between all fissures which you wish to use to trigger the explosion. A path between fissures is formed by making sure that all the dirt connecting the fissures is at the same level. Note that if the antiquity is located anywhere within the path of the detonation, it will be immediately destroyed and you will have to start the excavation again. This skill is therefore best used once you have already finished digging up the antiquity and are hunting for bonus loot.

If you have the second Hand Brush upgrade, it is possible to store up to 4 intuition and therefore use the trowel to dig six layers down in one go. This makes it even more important to calculate the layers of dirt remaining and so avoid damaging the antiquity. Higher level antiquities are especially delicate and can be damaged in one hit.

[[File:ON-icon-book-grimoire-Bow.png|right]]
:''Fire a burst at your feet while flipping backwards 15 meters.  Casting again within 4 seconds increases the cost by 33%.''

'''Vault''' is a Scribed skill Grimoire, on the [[ON:Bow|Bow]] skill line.  It can be purchased after earning the [[ON:Bow Master|Bow Master]] achievement from [[ON:Chronicler Firandil|Chronicler Firandil]] in [[ON:The Scholarium|the Scholarium]] once per character. 
It costs {{ESO Price|50,000}} the first time, and {{ESO Price|10,000}} for other characters on your account after that.  The name of the scribed skill changes depending upon your choice of Focus Script.

In order to use this skill effectively, you need to pay attention to what's behind you in order to avoid falling off a cliff or into another hazard, or alerting more enemies.  The safest thing to do may be to maneuver yourself so that your back is to a wall.  You can also take advantage of the fact that you generally cannot jump to a higher elevation than where you started.  So casting the skill while facing downwards on a slope or stairway will prevent you from going too far back when flipping.  Also be aware that the skill has a tendency to double-cast (most likely because you cast it while still in the middle of another attack animation, so you don't jump immediately and press the key twice not realizing that the first cast was just delayed).  So in locations where falling off the edge is a real danger (e.g. boss fights in the [[ON:Infinite Archive|Infinite Archive]]), you might want to avoid using this skill at all.

*Radius: 6 meters

Online:Traveling Knife:
{{Trail|Scribing}}
[[File:ON-icon-book-grimoire-Dual Wield.png|right]]
:''Twirl and throw an enchanted dagger at an enemy, which returns to you after a short delay and hits additional enemies in the path.''

'''Traveling Knife''' is a Scribed skill Grimoire, on the [[ON:Dual Wield|Dual Wield]] skill line.  It can be purchased after earning the [[ON:Dual Wield Master|Dual Wield Master]] achievement from [[ON:Chronicler Firandil|Chronicler Firandil]] in [[ON:The Scholarium|the Scholarium]] once per character.

It costs {{ESO Price|50,000}} the first time, and {{ESO Price|10,000}} for other characters on your account after that.  The name of the scribed skill changes depending upon your choice of Focus Script.

Traveling Knife causes you to throw a knife at an enemy target, which causes damage to the target, and then to any enemies between the target and you on return (except for Shattering Knife, which damages other enemies around the target instead).  The exact effects depend on your choice of scripts.

The trick to using this skill is that in order to get the most effect from it, you want to target the most distant opponent in a group, so that it hits as many other targets as possible on the way back.  This can be difficult as the game generally wants to prioritize closer targets.  You can of course move between the throw and the return to line up more potential targets.  One thing to note is that you always throw with your right hand and catch with your left.  This means that it's easier to throw to the right side of the closer targets and then move to the left than it is to do the reverse.  (Shattering Knife makes this irrelevant, of course.)

*Cast Time: Instant
*Target: Enemy
*Range: 15 meters

{{Trail|Scribing}}
[[File:ON-icon-book-grimoire-Assault.png|right]]
:''Pierce the air with a shrill whistle, calling your mount forth to trample enemies in a line.  This ability cannot be re-activated while your mount is already attacking.''

'''Trample''' is a [[ON:Scribing|Scribed]] skill [[ON:Scribing#Grimoires|Grimoire]] on the [[ON:Assault|Assault]] skill line.  It can be purchased after earning the [[ON:Alliance War Skill Master|Alliance War Skill Master]] achievement from [[ON:Chronicler Firandil|Chronicler Firandil]] in [[ON:The Scholarium|the Scholarium]] once per character.

It costs {{ESO Price|50,000}} the first time, and {{ESO Price|10,000}} for other characters on your account after that.  The name of the scribed skill changes depending upon your choice of Focus Script.

Trample will call your active [[ON:Mounts|Mount]] to run forward from your position in a line, damaging all enemies in its path.  The other effects will depend upon your choice of scripts.  It works with all mounts, even the toy stick mounts, but the effects are the same regardless.

*Cast Time: 1.5 seconds.
*Target: Area
*Radius: 5 meters
*Duration: 2 seconds

'''Werewolf Transformation''' transforms you into a [[Online:Werewolf|Werewolf]].  This transformation will cause up to 3 nearby enemies to flee in terror. Passively increases your {{ESO Stamina Link||Recovery}} while slotted. While in Werewolf form, you will take increased damage from [[ON:Poison Damage|Poison]]. Outside combat, there will be no {{ESO Ultimate Link}} drain to maintain the transformation. However, once in combat it will cost {{ESO Ultimate Link|100}} every ten seconds to maintain the form.

While transformed and in combat, used werewolf abilities will generate 15 Fury each time and the progress bar can be found on the left hand side of the ability bar. Fury does not decay, but when you leave the transformation any built-up Fury will be lost.

Once the Fury reaches 1,000, the Ultimate ability will transform into {{icon|skill|Werewolf-Rampage|30}}[[ON:Rampage|Rampage]], and has the following description:
:''Consume your fury and unleash the beast, increasing your Movement Speed by 20%, damage done by 15%, and reducing the cost of your Werewolf Transformation and abilities by 100% for 20 seconds. This effect is lost if you leave Werewolf form.''

The '''Pack Leader''' morph, you will summon two direwolves to fight at your side dealing [[ON:Physical Damage|Physical Damage]]. Your block mitigation increases by 30% and you gain [[ON:Major Protection|Major Protection]] while transformed. You and your allies will also gain a [[Online:Minor Courage|Minor Courage]] buff. Additionally Rampage will be upgraded to "Enduring Rampage" which adds {{ESO Health Link||Recovery}} to its base effects.

The '''Werewolf Berserker''' morph will add [[ON:Bleed Damage|Bleed Damage]] to your Light and Heavy attacks, along with a [[ON:Major Berserk|Major Berserk]] buff to yourself. The morph also upgrades the [[Online:Insatiable Hunger|Insatiable Hunger]] so it also generates Fury when used.
{{NewLeft}}
==Notes==
* Werewolf Transformation is provided to you at no skill point cost when earning the Werewolf skill line.
* While transformed you're locked into only using your Werewolf abilities.
* You can go back to your humanoid form at any time by using Werewolf Transformation while transformed. In both transformations, you stun yourself for 1 second while being immune to all other crowd controls.{{vn|is this true post Update 50"}}
* Werewolf Transformation and its morphs passively increase your {{ESO Stamina Link||Recovery}} while slotted even when not transformed.
* The updated werewolf models from [[ON:Update 50|Update 50]] now show [[Lore:Sexual Dimorphism|Sexual Dimorphism]]. The female model is slightly slimmer, with a longer tail, smaller ears, shorter snout and more fur on their chests compared to the male model.
**When the Rampage ability is ready to be used, glowing runes will appear on the werewolf's arms. Green if it is a Pack Leader and red if it is a Berserker.

* The Pack Leader's two direwolves appear in random variations. They can be either as ice wolves, red pit wolves, or doom wolves.
* The Pack Leader's Minor Courage buff affects group members within 30 meters.

{{ESO Patch Note|12.0.5|*Werewolf Transformation:
**This Ultimate and its morphs have been largely reworked in regards to how they function to cast and manage. These Ultimates now only require 100 Ultimate to activate but will continue to drain 100 Ultimate every 10 seconds while they are active. Failing to have 100 Ultimate when the cost per tick occurs will forcibly de-transform you. The cost to maintain transformation is now completely disabled outside of combat, to help mitigate the need to constantly engage in combat. Ultimate generation is no longer disabled while transformed, making it the primary method of sustaining your form.
**Completely rescripted the backend of the transformation, resulting in all Werewolf effects and passives to only apply while Transformed and a college dissertation level of data structuring changes, rather than applying permanently and constantly checking if you’re in Werewolf form. This should have no observable changes in behavior (unless called out otherwise in further sections), and is largely non-player facing and only aims at helping cut down on combat calculations for Werewolf characters (we saved 15 whole effects, which is a new record). However, if you experience issues where you lose access to passives or other effects while in Werewolf form, please let us know!
**Transforming into a Werewolf no longer increases your Maximum Stamina by 30%. Instead, all Werewolf abilities that scale with Stamina or Magicka will now be 30% more dense in their scaling, allowing for similar levels of combat power as before, without the added bonus of having a deeper resource pool.
**Reduced the Poison damage taken while transformed to 10%, down from 25%.
**Werewolf Stamina costing abilities (aside from the core combat mechanics such as Block, Bash, Dodge, or Prowl) now cost 1/3rd of their ability category counterpart, rather than costing 25% more. This was done to help open more potential build opportunities for non-Stamina damage dealers to utilize Werewolf, while also adding to the sensation that this Ultimate is a transformation that makes you more powerful in some capacity. The cost is now almost exclusively on maintaining the form, rather than the form and your normal resources – helping simplify its combat loop and letting you focus while the beast is unleashed.
**Werewolf combat actions no longer see a 15% damage increase in their scaling. We’ll cover this more in each ability, but fear not, Werewolves are stronger than they were before in most cases with some other adjustments.
**The unique bar that activates while in Werewolf form has been reworked to house a new mechanic, called “Fury”. Fury is a unique resource that generates from activating Werewolf abilities while in combat. It stores up to 1000, and each ability activated grants 15 at base. Fury does not decay, but leaving Werewolf form will result in losing all built-up Fury. Morphs and passives both can expedite the amount of Fury generated or can even add more forms of generating it. While you have 1000 Fury, your Ultimate ability will be replaced with “Rampage.” Activating Rampage drains all Fury and grants you a 20 second window of increased power, increasing your Movement Speed by 20%, damage done by 15%, and removes the cost of all Werewolf abilities, including the Transformation. Activating Rampage will temporarily disable your ability to activate the Werewolf Transformation again, to create the sensation of loss of control to this inner beast, as well as making it harder to accidentally activate and immediately lose the effect if you input the button multiple times and de-transform.
**Werewolf Light Attacks no longer have their base damage capped at 4813 like other Light Attacks, in efforts to help add more potential damage while transformed.
***Werewolf Berserker: This morph now grants Major Berserk while transformed. Updated the Bleed from this morph to apply on Light and Heavy Attacks, rather than only Light Attacks. The Bleed now appears to stack up to 5 times in total and upon reaching 5 stacks, the 1 second delay will be removed, allowing you to deal much more consistent damage while sticking to a target. Stacks do not augment damage or duration. {{ESO Patch Note|9.1.5|*This passive now increases your damage done by 2/5% against enemies within 15 meters of you and increases your Critical Chance by 657/1314 against enemies that are further than 15 meters from you, rather than increasing your damage done with Bow attacks by 6/12% based on how far away you are
*Renamed this passive to "Vinedusk Training" to accurately adjust its implications to its new functionality, with a flavorful lore twist.
**''Developer Comment: In order to help Bows feel more like additional tools for your character rather than their own isolated play style, we're expanding out this bonus two-fold to help it become a more viable option for different builds. Since this passive previously only enhanced other Bow attacks, it created situations where the weapon heavily dissuaded you to use other skills, making it feel restrictive rather than additive. By opening the bonus to work with any attack, we hope to help it feel more like other weapons as a way to synergize and play off your other actions. In addition, this passive's mini game was creating situations that heavily punished many different encounters both in PvP and PvE, where you had to maximize your range at all times from the target. By granting two individual bonuses for close range and further range, we can help enable more consistent power to the weapon, each with their own advantages, without creating frustrating game play experiences that further harmed synergy with other actions like class skills or group coordination.''}}
